reference_opening.argument: This video is scam content because the creator promotes Forsage Xqore as a way to make money, claims that participation yields a 50% distribution, and encourages viewers to join the system. The description supplies a personal Forsage ID link, indicating a referral destination connected to the promoted money-making program rather than neutral reporting or testing. The video does not present criticism, investigation, or contrary context that would qualify the solicitation.

citations.quote: Farsage's XCore program distributes 50% in the community
50% will be distributed in your planner's team
We wish you to be part of this beautiful system
we will work together and earn a good amount of money
How To Make Money Forsage Xqore

opening.argument: Judge, the speaker describes how the program works, but does not promise a certain payout. His closing hope that participants will earn is expressly conditional: “If Allah wills.” The 50% statement describes a distribution within the program; it does not establish that any viewer will receive a particular amount or profit. The invitation to participate should be read alongside that uncertainty, not converted into a guaranteed-return claim.

citations.quote: I'm going to give you information about Farsage's Program
Farsage's XCore program distributes 50% in the community
If Allah wills we will work together and earn a good amount of money.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The prosecution is right to identify an invitation and an ID link, but neither quote establishes a guaranteed return or explains what a viewer must pay to join. “50%” is presented as a distribution, while the speaker's expectation of earnings is conditional. Those distinctions matter when deciding whether this is a deceptive money-making pitch rather than an enthusiastic explanation.

citations.quote: My Forsage Id Link: ...
Farsage's XCore program distributes 50% in the community
If Allah wills we will work together and earn a good amount of money.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: Conditional phrasing does not undo the solicitation. The speaker invites viewers into the system, describes money going to a participant and their team, and anticipates earning together. A guaranteed amount is not necessary to recognize the promoted team-based earning mechanism.

citations.quote: 50% you will get, 50% you will get to you and 50% will be distributed in your planner's team.
We wish you to be part of this beautiful system, If Allah wills we will work together and earn a good amount of money.

opening.argument: Judge, the segment is organized as a short explanation of a program, not a walkthrough of signing up or sending money. The speaker says he will give information, enumerates the program variants, and identifies XCore as the focus. Even the discussion of the 50% distribution can be read as explaining a feature. The closing invitation is promotional, but it does not erase the informational substance of the presentation.

citations.quote: I'm going to give you information about Farsage's Program which has 5 basic programs
The basic of today's basics video about XCore
Farsage's XCore program distributes 50% in the community
We wish you to be part of this beautiful system

rebuttal.rebuttal: The title's money-making language and the description's ID link give the explanation a promotional context, but they do not show an enrollment transaction or a required payment. Nor does the quoted distribution explain what produces the money. The prosecution's reading treats an overview of program features as sufficient proof of a scam mechanism.

citations.quote: How To Make Money Forsage Xqore
My Forsage Id Link: ...
Farsage's XCore program distributes 50% in the community

true_side_reply.rebuttal: An explanatory format does not make the content neutral. The explanation centers on a distribution to the viewer and their team, then asks viewers to become part of the system and earn money together. The personal ID link reinforces that the overview functions as promotion.

citations.quote: 50% you will get, 50% you will get to you and 50% will be distributed in your planner's team.
We wish you to be part of this beautiful system, If Allah wills we will work together and earn a good amount of money.
My Forsage Id Link: ...

opening.argument: Judge, the visible evidence supports a program promotion with a personal ID link and a described community distribution. It does not establish the terms of joining, a required deposit, or that participants are paid for recruiting others. “Your planner's team” identifies where the speaker says part of the distribution goes, but does not explain what generates it. A referral-style promotion is not, by itself, proof that the arrangement is a recruitment-funded scam.

citations.quote: My Forsage Id Link: ...
Farsage's XCore program distributes 50% in the community
50% will be distributed in your planner's team.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The prosecution connects the ID link, the team distribution, and the invitation. That establishes promotion, but the cited words do not say viewers earn by recruiting, identify a payment required to enter, or trace the source of the distributed funds. The team reference alone cannot settle those missing mechanics.

citations.quote: My Forsage Id Link: ...
50% will be distributed in your planner's team.
We wish you to be part of this beautiful system

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The defense isolates each clue, but the video presents them together: a personal ID link, a claimed share for the viewer and their team, and an invitation to join and earn. The precise source of funds is not explained; that absence does not make the team-based money-making solicitation an ordinary loyalty offer.
